subject.title: Matrix exec approvals: edit expired prompts instead of redacting them (avoid tombstone clutter, keep audit trail)

question: Should expired Matrix execution approvals preserve the original command in the room as an edited terminal state, or should the secure default remain redaction?
rationale: The change improves auditability and removes tombstones, but it deliberately retains potentially sensitive execution text in a shared channel and no existing documented contract establishes the preferred default.

options.title: Use edited expiry state
options.body: Make expiry update the original prompt to a compact expired state, preserve the command under the existing approval visibility policy, and remove stale reactions.

options.title: Keep redaction
options.body: Retain the current privacy-oriented expiry behavior and document why expired approval contents must not persist in Matrix rooms.

options.title: Add an explicit policy
options.body: Introduce a narrowly documented Matrix expiry policy only if maintainers need different retention behavior across deployments.

recommendation.title: Use edited expiry state
recommendation.body: Make expiry update the original prompt to a compact expired state, preserve the command under the existing approval visibility policy, and remove stale reactions.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a secure-default and product-policy choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.
